clue.text: Olympian English family raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are written upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: An English family raised in sport, perhaps producing an Olympic athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns EKIN upwards. 'Olympian' looks like an athlete but means a god of Olympus; Nike was the Greek goddess of victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Nike was the winged goddess of victory, one of the deities dwelling on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Division in church exists between ends of spectrum

indicators.note: the church and exists letters go between the two end letters, so they sit inside
the ends of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: its first and last letters are S and M
exists means is

explanation.surface: A church split spanning the whole range of opinion, from one end of the spectrum to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division, especially within a religious body.

clue.text: Where I keep something secret (not my hand)

definitions.text: Where I keep something secret (not my hand)

parts.words: Where I keep something secret (not my hand)
parts.note: the idiom for keeping a plan hidden in reserve, with the card-sharp's hiding place in mind; the bracket rules out the other card idiom about holding cards close

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not my hand' steers away from 'close to my chest' or a hand of cards; the phrase wanted is the conjuror's or cheat's hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Having something hidden in one's clothing at the wrist is the idiom for a secret resource kept in reserve.

clue.text: A bachelor pursued by so-called queen, leader in sisterhood?

indicators.note: the first pieces are followed, chased, by the next, so the queen comes after

parts.note: Good Queen Bess was the nickname of Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: A single man is chased by a self-styled queen bee, the leader of a sisterhood.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess is the head of a community of nuns, a religious sisterhood; the question mark admits the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Reflective quality about top spy mystery, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mirror-like quality surrounding a spymaster's strange mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a call for odd letters, but here it signals a rearrangement of M plus MYSTERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Symmetry is correspondence of the two halves, as in a mirror image, so it is a quality of reflection.

clue.text: Son allowed to do survey

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
if you are allowed to do something, you can

explanation.surface: A son is given permission to carry out a survey.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to look over or examine quickly, the same as surveying.

clue.text: Indicator of tense change in excited raptor, such as a hawk

indicators.note: the tense marker goes inside the shuffled letters
excited letters are stirred up, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the ending -ed changes a verb to past tense

explanation.surface: A grammar point embedded in an agitated bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raptor' tempts as the definition, since a hawk is one, but it is the fodder; the past-tense ending is the inserted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawk hunts and kills other creatures for food, so it is an example of a predator.

clue.text: Divine female with one sibling

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
sis is short for sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: A godlike woman with a single brother or sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the chief goddess of ancient Egyptian religion.

clue.text: Recast the three leading characters in play, not well

indicators.note: to recast is to rework or remould, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the first three letters of the alphabet are A, B and C

explanation.surface: A director recasts the three lead roles in a play that went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre talk hides an alphabet: the 'leading characters' are letters, not actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something incapably means doing it without competence, which is doing it badly.

clue.text: Venerated female heard but not seen in programmes

indicators.note: the word for programmes is said aloud, but the written form differs

parts.note: a series is a set of broadcast programmes

explanation.surface: A revered woman who is listened to on air but never appears on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceres was the Roman goddess of agriculture, a deity worshipped by her followers.

clue.text: Name of David's girlfriend — but her heart wasn't in it

definitions.text: Name of David's girlfriend — but her heart wasn't in it

parts.words: Name of David's girlfriend — but her heart wasn't in it
parts.note: David Copperfield's childhood sweetheart is Little Em'ly, whose name is printed with its middle letter missing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Her heart wasn't in it' sounds like reluctance, but it is literal: Dickens spells her Em'ly, with the central letter dropped. The theme also points to Emily Brontë.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's David Copperfield, Little Em'ly is the hero's early love; her full given name is the answer.

clue.text: Furious triad of Brussels bureaucrats ahead of a fateful day?

indicators.note: the bureaucrats come before the day in the answer

parts.note: EU for the European Union, based in Brussels, plus MEN
the Ides of March was the day Julius Caesar was assassinated

explanation.surface: Three angry Eurocrats meet before some doom-laden date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furious' looks like plain anger but points to the Furies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eumenides is a euphemistic Greek name for the Furies, the three goddesses of vengeance.

clue.text: Does, for example, what's wrong in France, cutting wages

indicators.note: the French word cuts into, so goes inside, the wages

parts.note: fees are payments for work
mal is French for evil or wrong

explanation.surface: Something is amiss in France, with pay being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' is not the verb but the plural of doe, female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Does are female deer, so they are examples of the sex that bears young.

clue.text: Honours, we hear, those dealing with life and death matters

definitions.text: those dealing with life and death matters

indicators.note: signals that the word for honours is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to fete someone is to honour or celebrate them

explanation.surface: Awards, so people say, go to those in life-or-death professions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fates of Greek myth were three goddesses who spun, measured and cut the thread of each mortal life.

clue.text: Scene of drama — in which masked man wields knife

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a playhouse where plays are staged

definitions.text: in which masked man wields knife
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an operating room, where a masked surgeon cuts

explanation.surface: A dramatic scene in which a masked assailant brandishes a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: The masked knifeman sounds like a villain on stage, but he is a surgeon in an operating room.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a playhouse and, in British usage, a hospital operating room.

clue.text: Removed in period prescribed, but not the first time

parts.note: an era is a period of history

indicators.note: the first occurrence of the time letter is left out

parts.note: dictated means laid down or prescribed

explanation.surface: Something taken off a course of medication within the stated period, though not on the first occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first T of DICTATED goes, leaving DICATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out or get rid of entirely, so eradicated means removed.

clue.text: 11's pen-name some embellished

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following word are used, a run lying inside it

parts.note: the run sits within this word

explanation.surface: A writer's pseudonym that has been somewhat dressed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is EMILY: Emily Brontë published as Ellis Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Brontë's pseudonym was Ellis Bell, with Ellis as the given name.

clue.text: What each little woman had in play

definitions.meaning: first meaning: each of the four March girls in Little Women has that many siblings
second meaning: Chekhov's drama about the Prozorov siblings

explanation.walkthrough: Little Women by Louisa May Alcott follows four sisters, so each has three; Chekhov's play shares the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Each March girl has three siblings, all girls, and Chekhov wrote a play of that title.

clue.text: Ruby embracing Victoria or Virginia, in other words

indicators.note: the colour holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: ruby is a shade of red
Victoria is an Australian state and Virginia a US state

explanation.surface: A woman called Ruby hugging another woman, Victoria or Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: The three names look like women but Victoria and Virginia are states, and Ruby a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Restated means expressed again, said a second time using different phrasing.

clue.text: eg 23, preceded by 17 21 in novel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Little Dorrit's first name, Dickens's heroine
second meaning: the youngest March girl in Little Women, born after her three siblings

explanation.walkthrough: 23 is DORRIT; Dickens's heroine is Amy Dorrit. 17 21 is THREE SISTERS: the youngest in Little Women came after Meg, Jo and Beth.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to Dickens's Little Dorrit and to the youngest March girl in Alcott's novel.

clue.text: Almost everyone protested in a way about a fierce dog

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: the outer letters go around the following a, enclosing it

parts.note: a sit-in is a way of protesting, so 'sat in' means protested

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone staged a protest about an aggressive dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A sit-in is a form of protest, so 'protested in a way' reads as sat in; the A goes near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alsatian, or German shepherd, is a large breed often used as a guard dog.

clue.text: Name first of female trio, annually

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a girl's given name
second meaning: the opening month of three each year that double as girls' names, followed by May and June

explanation.walkthrough: The 'female trio' is three consecutive months that are also girls' names, recurring each year.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name and the first of three successive calendar months that are also women's names.

clue.text: See 17
Arranged dowries as members of Shakespearean threesome?

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Marriage settlements set up for the members of a Shakespearean trio.
explanation.walkthrough: The trio is the three witches in Macbeth, the Weird Sisters; the question mark flags the jokey plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth's witches are called the Weird Sisters, so each is playfully one of the oddballs.

clue.text: Girl hiding sister's last tool

indicators.note: the girl conceals the letter within herself

parts.note: wench is an old word for a girl

indicators.note: the final letter of the sister word is the one taken here

parts.note: the possessive points to the word sister itself

explanation.surface: A girl conceals her sister's final tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a spanner, a hand tool for gripping and turning nuts and bolts.

clue.text: Novel heroine's passionate, with extreme letters exchanged

indicators.note: exchanged means the two end letters trade places with each other
the letters at the two extremes, first and last, are the ones in play

parts.note: torrid means passionate, as in a torrid affair

explanation.surface: A heroine of fiction is hot-blooded, writing with extreme language.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the T and D at the two ends of TORRID. Little Dorrit is Dickens's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy Dorrit is the title heroine of Dickens's novel Little Dorrit.

clue.text: Alcott and her characters represented as sweet

indicators.note: the letters of these words are presented again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Louisa May Alcott and her characters are depicted as sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like the people of her books but means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a pudding of fruit or custard baked or set in a mould lined with bread or sponge.

clue.text: Preserve line within large family

indicators.note: the line letter goes inside the preserve word

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins

explanation.surface: Keeping the bloodline going within a big family.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is an extended kinship group, especially in Scotland, descended from a common ancestor.

clue.text: 17 21 constituted issue for this tragic father

definitions.text: 17 21 constituted issue for this tragic father

parts.words: 17 21 constituted issue for this tragic father
parts.note: Shakespeare's tragic king had three daughters, Goneril, Regan and Cordelia, as his offspring

explanation.walkthrough: 17 21 is THREE SISTERS; 'issue' means offspring, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic king divides his realm among his three daughters, with disastrous results.

clue.text: Vessel carrying vital supply from China or Taiwan

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters across these words

parts.note: the letters run across china, or and taiwan

explanation.surface: A ship carrying essential goods from China or Taiwan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery, the blood vessel carrying oxygenated blood from the heart.

clue.text: Girl taking a course from Exeter to Leeds

parts.note: Leeds lies roughly north-north-east of Exeter, a compass bearing abbreviated NNE

explanation.surface: A girl sets off on a long journey from Exeter in Devon to Leeds in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a compass heading, not a route or a degree course.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne is a woman's given name, and also the youngest Brontë sister.

clue.text: Field and bowl

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sphere of activity
second meaning: a stadium, a bowl-shaped venue for sport

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cricket, fielding and bowling, but each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an area of activity or competition and an enclosed amphitheatre for contests.

clue.text: Growth man cut, in case

indicators.note: the cut word sits inside the word for case

parts.note: an action is a legal case or lawsuit

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A tumour that a man had excised is held in a specimen case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a verb, giving CREW, cut to CRE; 'case' is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Accretion is gradual growth by layers being added, as with sediment or deposits.
